text:
nova: hi all, first week here! trying to run the quickstart but my requests keep returning 401. i created a key from Console > API Keys but the header still fails. any common mistakes?

devex-lee: welcome :tada: common issues: 1) not including 'Bearer' in Authorization header, 2) copying extra whitespace/newline, 3) using the placeholder in the UI instead of rotating to reveal the real key. can you paste the exact curl (redact the key)?

nova: heres what i tried:
```
curl -H "Authorization: sk-sandbox_ABCDEF" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

riah: aha you need the 'Bearer' prefix:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-sandbox_ABCDEF" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

nova: oh wow thanks. small thing but took me a while. another question: what's the difference between sandbox and hosted keys?

corey (infra): sandbox keys are tenant-isolated keys intended for dev/test. hosted/prod keys are provisioned for paid accounts and have higher quotas and SLAs. sandbox keys are logged to our dev telemetry and are subject to sandbox rate limits.

sam (policy): to add: sandbox keys cannot access Private deployment endpoints or dedicated clusters. they only hit hosted public inference planes. also sandbox keys are rate-limited to 40 requests/minute by default and 50k tokens/day for new hires.

nova: is there a way to get a temporary higher rate for a demo?

devex-lee: yes, file a Support -> Quota Request and request an elevated sandbox tier for the demo window. include start/end times and expected token counts. approvals for small demos are usually same-day.

nova: where can i monitor if i'm hitting the limit?

corey (infra): Console -> Usage shows per-key RPS and token breakdown. 429 responses include x-rate-limit headers with remaining and reset. if you see persistent 429s we can also enable a short burst window.

nova: perfect. last nit: any onboarding cheat-sheet for env setup?

onboarding-bot: Onboarding checklist: 1) Create sandbox key in Console -> API Keys 2) Set REDWOOD_API_KEY in local env 3) Run quickstart (links) 4) Request quota increases if necessary 5) Join #devex for help.

riah: we also have a tiny repo with examples for node/python/ruby under gitlab.com/redwood/examples. use the secrets manager snippet for CI.

nova: thanks everyone, this saved my morning :heart:
